html:
A famine that struck the Ethiopian Empire from 1888 to 1892, remembered in Ethiopia as the "evil days". Estimates of the dead run as high as a third of the population, though no one counted.

Several blows fell at once. The rinderpest epidemic killed most of the cattle, including the oxen that pulled the ploughs, so fields went unsown. Drought, locusts and caterpillars destroyed crops. Cholera, typhus and smallpox followed the hunger.

War made it worse. Armies of the Mahdist State of Sudan raided the west, and Emperor Yohannes IV was killed fighting them in 1889. Italy was pushing inland from its colony on the Red Sea. Menelik II came to the throne in the middle of the disaster. Ethiopia recovered quickly enough to beat Italy at Adwa in 1896. Famine returned in the 20th century, most famously in the famine of 1983 to 1985.
sum: A famine that struck the Ethiopian Empire from 1888 to 1892, remembered in Ethiopia as the "evil days". Estimates of the dead run as high as a third of the population, though no one counted.
